title: Acts Done by Several Persons in Furtherance of Common Intention
old_text: When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone.
new_text: When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone.
punishment_old: Rule of joint constructive liability (punished according to the principal offence committed).
punishment_new: Constructive joint liability maintained under general principles in sub-section 3(5).
explanation: IPC Section 34 stood as an independent section for joint criminal liability. In BNS, this principle has been subsumed into Section 3 as sub-section (5) under General Explanations.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 3(5)

title: Act of a Person of Unsound Mind (Insanity Defence)
old_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law.
new_text: Nothing is an offence which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or that he is doing what is either wrong or contrary to law.
punishment_old: Complete statutory general defence (acquittal / institutional treatment under CrPC).
punishment_new: Complete statutory general defence (maintained under BNSS provisions).
explanation: The classic McNaghten legal insanity defence remains substantively unchanged in text and scope, but is renumbered from IPC Section 84 to BNS Section 22.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 22

title: Things Done in Private Defence
old_text: Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.
new_text: Nothing is an offence which is done in the exercise of the right of private defence.
punishment_old: General defence excluding criminal culpability.
punishment_new: General defence excluding criminal culpability.
explanation: IPC Section 96, which established the foundational right of private defence of person and property, is renumbered to Section 34 of BNS with similar threshold limits.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 34

title: Acts Endangering Sovereignty, Unity and Integrity of India (Replacing Sedition)
old_text: Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or otherwise, brings or attempts to bring into hatred or contempt, or excites or attempts to excite disaffection towards the Government established by law in India, shall be punished...
new_text: Whoever, purposely or knowingly, by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or by electronic communication or by use of financial mean, or otherwise, excites or attempts to excite, secession or armed rebellion or subversive activities, or encourages feelings of separatist activities or endangers sovereignty or unity and integrity of India...
punishment_old: Imprisonment for life, to which fine may be added, or imprisonment up to 3 years, to which fine may be added, or fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life or with imprisonment which may extend to 7 years, and shall also be liable to fine.
explanation: The colonial term 'sedition' (rajdroh) is formally omitted. In its place, Section 152 penalizes acts endangering sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India (deshdroh), expanding means to include electronic communication and financial means, with mandatory minimum imprisonment raised from 3 to 7 years up to life.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 152

title: Unlawful Assembly
old_text: An assembly of five or more persons is designated an 'unlawful assembly', if the common object of the persons composing that assembly is...
new_text: An assembly of five or more persons is designated an 'unlawful assembly', if the common object of the persons composing that assembly is to overawe by criminal force, resist execution of law, commit mischief or trespass...
punishment_old: Definition section; punishable under IPC Section 143 with imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Punishable under BNS Section 189(2) with imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both.
explanation: Definition and five ingredients of unlawful assembly remain structurally unchanged, shifted from IPC 141 to BNS Section 189(1).
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 189

title: Punishment for Rioting
old_text: Whoever is guilty of rioting, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Whoever is guilty of rioting, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
explanation: Rioting definition and penalty are unified under Section 191 of BNS, where subsection (1) defines rioting (formerly IPC 146) and subsection (2) specifies punishment (formerly IPC 147).
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 191

title: Promoting Enmity Between Different Groups on Grounds of Religion, Race, Place of Birth
old_text: Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs or by visible representations or otherwise, promotes or attempts to promote feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities...
new_text: Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs or by visible representations or through electronic means or otherwise, promotes or attempts to promote feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different religious, racial, language or regional groups or castes or communities...
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both (up to 5 years if committed in place of worship).
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both (up to 5 years if committed in place of worship).
explanation: IPC Section 153A moved to BNS Section 196. The provision explicitly modernizes the medium to include 'through electronic communication' within the statutory text.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 196

title: Rash Driving or Riding on a Public Way
chapter: Offences Affecting Public Health, Safety, and Decency
old_text: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished...
new_text: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished...
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both.
explanation: Rash driving on public ways has been renumbered from IPC 279 to BNS Section 281. Note that causing death by rash driving (hit-and-run) is separately dealt with in BNS Section 106.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 281

title: Culpable Homicide
old_text: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide.
new_text: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide.
punishment_old: Definition section. Punishable under IPC Section 304.
punishment_new: Definition section. Punishable under BNS Section 105.
explanation: The core definition and trio of mental states (intention to kill, intention to cause bodily injury likely to cause death, knowledge of likelihood of death) moved from IPC 299 to BNS Section 100.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 100

title: Murder Definition and Exceptions
old_text: Except in the cases hereinafter excepted, culpable homicide is murder, if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death...
new_text: Except in the cases hereinafter excepted, culpable homicide is murder, if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death...
punishment_old: Definition section (with 5 exceptions). Punishable under IPC 302.
punishment_new: Definition section (with 5 exceptions). Punishable under BNS 103(1).
explanation: The foundational definition of murder with the 4 clauses and 5 exceptions (grave & sudden provocation, private defence excess, public servant, sudden fight, consent) is renumbered from IPC 300 to BNS Section 101.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 101

title: Punishment for Murder
old_text: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Death penalty or imprisonment for life, and liable to fine.
punishment_new: Death penalty or imprisonment for life, and liable to fine.
explanation: Perhaps the most famous section number in Indian legal history, Section 302 IPC has been renumbered to Section 103(1) of BNS. Subsection 103(2) introduces a new provision for mob lynching.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 103(1)

title: Murder by Group / Mob Lynching on Specified Grounds
old_text: No dedicated sub-clause in IPC. Prosecuted under Section 302 read with Section 34 or Section 149 of IPC.
new_text: When a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on the ground of race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other similar ground, each member of such group shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Not separately codified; charged under IPC 302 + 149/34.
punishment_new: Death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
explanation: A brand new provision codifying hate-motivated group murder and mob lynching on grounds of caste, community, personal belief, race, etc., with equal liability on all participants.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 103(2)

title: Dowry Death
old_text: Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called 'dowry death'...
new_text: Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called 'dowry death'...
punishment_old: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than 7 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than 7 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life.
explanation: IPC Section 304B has been shifted from homicide chapter to Chapter V (Offences Against Women and Children) and renumbered as Section 80 of BNS without reducing penalties or altering the 7-year statutory presumption window.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 80

title: Attempt to Murder
old_text: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished...
new_text: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished...
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine; if hurt caused, up to life imprisonment or 10 years.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine; if hurt caused, up to life imprisonment or 10 years.
explanation: The well-known Section 307 IPC for attempt to murder is renumbered to Section 109 of BNS, retaining identical legal standards for intention and hurt thresholds.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 109

title: Punishment for Voluntarily Causing Hurt
old_text: Whoever, except in the case provided for by section 334, voluntarily causes hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
new_text: Whoever, except in the case provided for by sub-section (1) of section 122, voluntarily causes hurt, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to 1,000 rupees, or both.
explanation: Simple hurt definition (IPC 319) and punishment (IPC 323) are consolidated under Section 115 of BNS as subsections (1) and (2).
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 115

title: Voluntarily Causing Hurt by Dangerous Weapons or Means
old_text: Whoever, except in the case provided for by section 334, voluntarily causes hurt by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death...
new_text: Whoever, voluntarily causes hurt by means of any instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any instrument which, used as a weapon of offence, is likely to cause death...
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
explanation: Hurt caused by dangerous weapons is reclassified under BNS Section 117 alongside grievous hurt classifications.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 117

title: Assault or Criminal Force to Woman with Intent to Outrage her Modesty
old_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished...
new_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman, intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage her modesty, shall be punished...
punishment_old: Imprisonment not less than 1 year which may extend to 5 years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment not less than 1 year which may extend to 5 years, and shall also be liable to fine.
explanation: IPC Section 354 has been renumbered to BNS Section 74, positioned at the start of Chapter V dedicated to crimes against women and children.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 74

title: Sexual Harassment
old_text: A man committing any of the following acts: physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; or a demand or request for sexual favours; or showing pornography against the will of a woman; or making sexually coloured remarks, shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment.
new_text: A man committing any of the following acts: physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures; or a demand or request for sexual favours; or showing pornography against the will of a woman; or making sexually coloured remarks, shall be guilty of the offence of sexual harassment.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both for clauses (i)-(iii); up to 1 year or fine or both for clause (iv).
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both for clauses (i)-(iii); up to 1 year or fine or both for clause (iv).
explanation: IPC 354A definitions and penalties directly mapped to BNS Section 75.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 75

title: Voyeurism
old_text: Any man who watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed...
new_text: Any man who watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed...
punishment_old: First conviction: 1 to 3 years and fine; Second/subsequent conviction: 3 to 7 years and fine.
punishment_new: First conviction: 1 to 3 years and fine; Second/subsequent conviction: 3 to 7 years and fine.
explanation: Voyeurism moves from IPC Section 354C to BNS Section 77 without alteration of punishment or scope.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 77

title: Stalking
old_text: Any man who follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest; or monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email or other form of electronic communication...
new_text: Any man who follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest; or monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email or other form of electronic communication...
punishment_old: First conviction: up to 3 years and fine; Subsequent conviction: up to 5 years and fine.
punishment_new: First conviction: up to 3 years and fine; Subsequent conviction: up to 5 years and fine.
explanation: Stalking (both physical and cyber stalking) moved from IPC 354D to BNS Section 78.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 78

title: Punishment for Rape
old_text: Whoever, except in the cases provided for in sub-section (2), commits rape, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Whoever, except in the cases provided for in sub-section (2), commits rape, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years extending to life, and fine. Aggravated cases up to remainder of natural life or death.
punishment_new: Rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years extending to life, and fine. Enhanced penalties for gang rape and rape of minors in subsequent sections (Sections 65-70).
explanation: Rape definition (IPC 375) and base punishment (IPC 376) are renumbered as BNS Section 63 and Section 64. Major restructuring divides aggravated forms into distinct sections (e.g. gang rape under Section 70, child rape under Section 65).
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 64

title: Punishment for Kidnapping
old_text: Whoever kidnaps any person from India or from lawful guardianship, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Whoever kidnaps any person from India or from lawful guardianship, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and liable to fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and liable to fine.
explanation: Kidnapping definitions and punishments consolidated under Section 137 of BNS, where subsection (2) prescribes general kidnapping punishment.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 137

title: Unnatural Offences
old_text: Whoever voluntarily has carnal intercourse against the order of nature with any man, woman or animal, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: No direct equivalent section retained in BNS. Consensual adult same-sex acts were previously decriminalised in Navtej Johar (2018). Bestiality and non-consensual acts against adult men are covered under broader assault or animal protection laws.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for life, or imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Section omitted in its historical form. Non-consensual acts against adult male victims are subject of parliamentary discussion (TODO: verify proposed amendments).
explanation: IPC Section 377 has been omitted from the BNS. After the Supreme Court struck down Section 377 regarding consenting adults in Navtej Singh Johar (2018), the lawmakers chose not to recreate a direct equivalent, though questions remain on non-consensual adult male coverage.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Legislative Debates & Omission

title: Punishment for Theft
old_text: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both; and in case of theft, where the value of stolen property is less than five thousand rupees, and a person is convicted for the first time, upon return of value or property, the court may sentence him to community service.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both; first-time theft under ₹5,000 may be punished with community service.
explanation: IPC Section 379 moved to BNS Section 303(2). A major statutory innovation is the introduction of 'Community Service' as an alternative punishment for first-time offenders where the stolen property value is below ₹5,000.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 303(2)

title: Snatching (New Specified Offence)
old_text: No distinct section in IPC. Handled as theft (Section 379) or robbery (Section 390) depending on whether force was used.
new_text: Theft is 'snatching' if, in order to commit theft, the offender suddenly or quickly or forcibly seizes, secures, grabs or takes away from any person or from his possession, any movable property.
punishment_old: Prosecuted under IPC 379 (up to 3 years) or IPC 392 (up to 10 years).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine.
explanation: Recognizing the widespread street crime of chain, phone, and bag snatching, BNS creates an express, distinct offence of 'Snatching' in Section 304, bridging the gap between simple theft and violent robbery.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 304

title: Punishment for Extortion
old_text: Whoever commits extortion shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Whoever commits extortion shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
explanation: Extortion definition (IPC 383) and punishment (IPC 384) are paired in BNS Section 308 as subsections (1) and (2).
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 308

title: Punishment for Robbery
old_text: Whoever commits robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and, if the robbery be committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, the imprisonment may be extended to fourteen years.
new_text: Whoever commits robbery shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine; and, if the robbery be committed on the highway between sunset and sunrise, the imprisonment may be extended to fourteen years.
punishment_old: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine; up to 14 years on highway between sunset and sunrise.
punishment_new: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine; up to 14 years on highway between sunset and sunrise.
explanation: IPC Section 392 is consolidated into Section 309 of BNS, where subsection (2) contains the exact punishment structure including enhanced punishment for night highway robberies.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 309

title: Punishment for Dacoity
old_text: Whoever commits dacoity shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
new_text: Whoever commits dacoity shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment for life, or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine.
explanation: Dacoity (joint robbery by 5 or more persons) moved from IPC 391/395 to BNS Section 310.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 310

title: Organised Crime
old_text: No comprehensive general organized crime provision under IPC. State enactments like MCOCA, KCOCA, or specialized statutes (UAPA) were invoked.
new_text: Any continuing unlawful activity including kidnapping, robbery, vehicle theft, extortion, land grabbing, contract killing, economic offences, cyber-crimes having severe consequences, trafficking in persons, drugs or illicit goods, or weapons, or human trafficking for prostitution or ransom, by any member of a syndicate...
punishment_old: No central IPC provision; dependent on state special laws.
punishment_new: If death results: death or imprisonment for life, fine not less than ₹10 lakh. In other cases: not less than 5 years extending to life, fine not less than ₹5 lakh.
explanation: BNS introduces a sweeping central statutory provision against organized crime syndicates, eliminating the need to rely purely on state-level legislation (like MCOCA).
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 111

title: Punishment for Criminal Breach of Trust
old_text: Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both (enhanced maximum term).
explanation: Criminal breach of trust moves from IPC 406 to BNS Section 316(2). Crucially, the maximum prison sentence has been enhanced from 3 years under IPC to 5 years under BNS.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 316

title: Cheating and Dishonestly Inducing Delivery of Property
old_text: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed...
new_text: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed...
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 7 years, and shall also be liable to fine.
explanation: The quintessential 'Section 420' of Indian popular culture and criminal law is now Section 318(4) of BNS. The definition and ingredients of cheating remain identical.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 318

title: Punishment for Criminal Trespass
old_text: Whoever commits criminal trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both.
new_text: Whoever commits criminal trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three months, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to 500 rupees, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine up to 5,000 rupees, or both (fine amount updated).
explanation: Criminal trespass punishment is renumbered to BNS Section 329(3). The monetary fine ceiling has been updated from ₹500 to ₹5,000 to adjust for inflation.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 329

title: Husband or Relative of Husband of a Woman Subjecting Her to Cruelty
old_text: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. Explanation defines cruelty...
new_text: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine. [Detailed definition of cruelty split into Section 86]
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, and shall also be liable to fine.
explanation: Section 498A IPC has been bifurcated in BNS: Section 85 contains the offence and penalty, while Section 86 provides the comprehensive statutory definition of 'cruelty' (including mental and physical harm).
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 85 & 86

title: Punishment for Defamation
old_text: Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both or with community service.
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both, or with community service.
explanation: Defamation definition (IPC 499) and penalty (IPC 500) are merged into BNS Section 356. Importantly, 'Community Service' is now expressly added as an alternative sentencing option.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 356

title: Punishment for Criminal Intimidation
old_text: Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both; and if threat be to cause death or grievous hurt...
new_text: Whoever commits the offence of criminal intimidation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both; and if threat be to cause death or grievous hurt...
punishment_old: Up to 2 years, or fine, or both; if threat is death/grievous hurt, up to 7 years or fine or both.
punishment_new: Up to 2 years, or fine, or both; if threat is death/grievous hurt, up to 7 years or fine or both.
explanation: Definition (IPC 503) and punishment (IPC 506) are consolidated under Section 351 of BNS as subsections (1) and (2).
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 351

title: Word, Gesture or Act Intended to Insult the Modesty of a Woman
old_text: Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any word, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman...
new_text: Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any words, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman...
punishment_old: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine.
punishment_new: Simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine.
explanation: IPC 509 (eve-teasing and verbal harassment) is renumbered to Section 79 of BNS, placed in the dedicated women's protection chapter.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 79

title: Dishonestly Receiving Stolen Property
old_text: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen property, shall be punished...
new_text: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen property, shall be punished...
punishment_old: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
explanation: Definition of stolen property (IPC 410) and penalty for receiving it (IPC 411) are paired under BNS Section 317.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 317

title: Forgery
chapter: Offences Relating to Documents and Property Marks
old_text: Whoever makes any false documents or false electronic record or part of a document or electronic record, with intent to cause damage or injury, to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title...
new_text: Whoever makes any false documents or false electronic record or part of a document or electronic record, with intent to cause damage or injury, to the public or to any person, or to support any claim or title...
punishment_old: Definition section. Punishable under IPC Section 465 with imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Definition and basic punishment merged under BNS Section 336.
explanation: Forgery definitions and base punishment are consolidated under Section 336 of BNS, preserving digital and physical forgery classifications.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 336

title: Abetment of a Thing
old_text: A person abets the doing of a thing, who: First—Instigates any person to do that thing; or Secondly—Engages with one or more other person or persons in any conspiracy... or Thirdly—Intentionally aids, by any act or illegal omission...
new_text: A person abets the doing of a thing, who: First—Instigates any person to do that thing; or Secondly—Engages with one or more other person or persons in any conspiracy... or Thirdly—Intentionally aids, by any act or illegal omission...
punishment_old: General principle; punished as per the offence abetted under subsequent sections.
punishment_new: General principle; punished as per the offence abetted under subsequent sections.
explanation: The three classical limbs of abetment (instigation, conspiracy, intentional aid) moved from IPC 107 to BNS Section 45.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 45

title: Criminal Conspiracy
old_text: When two or more persons agree to do, or cause to be done: (1) an illegal act, or (2) an act which is not illegal by illegal means, such an agreement is designated a criminal conspiracy...
new_text: When two or more persons agree to do, or cause to be done: (1) an illegal act, or (2) an act which is not illegal by illegal means, such an agreement is designated a criminal conspiracy...
punishment_old: Under IPC 120B: punishable in the same manner as abetment of such offence, or up to 6 months/fine for lesser offences.
punishment_new: Under BNS 61(2): punishable in the same manner as if he had abetted such offence, or up to 6 months/fine.
explanation: Criminal conspiracy definition (IPC 120A) and punishment (IPC 120B) are consolidated into Section 61 of BNS.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 61

title: Causing Death by Negligence
old_text: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine; and if such act is done by a registered medical practitioner while performing medical procedure, he shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and shall also be liable to fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 5 years, and fine; doctors performing medical procedure capped at 2 years.
explanation: IPC 304A is substantially modified in BNS Section 106(1). The general punishment for causing death by negligence is raised from 2 years to 5 years, with a specific carve-out for registered medical practitioners capped at 2 years. Section 106(2) creates a dedicated 10-year penalty for hit-and-run drivers who flee.
source: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Section 106(1)
